newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Skala plans to acquire retailer Centrum.
newsitem.headline: Skala plans to acquire retailer Centrum.

text.p: Hungarian retail group Skala-Coop, a subsidiary of Germany's Tengelmann, applied for the permission of the Fair Competition Office to acquire a majority in retail chain Centrum Aruhazak Rt, Skala-Coop said on Tuesday.
Skala-Coop Rt has raised Centrum's capital and after the registration it will hold 43.5 percent in the firm, it said in the Budapest Stock Exchange's (BSE) official gazette.
Together with one of its subsidiaries, Skala-Coop will receive a majority stake in Centrum, pending the competition watchdog's permission, Skala-Coop added.
Skala-Coop Rt Chairman Istvan Imre told Reuters that according to finalised deals, the group would hold 52 to 53 percent of Centrum's shares.
He added that Skala-Coop raised Centrum's capital by one billion forints to some six billion.
Earlier he said that the capital increase would boost Skal-Coop's stake to 37 percent from 25 percent.
"But we have bought more shares since then," he told Reuters on Tuesday.
Imre said Skala-Coop planned to invest further billions of forints in Centrum, only adding that Skala was assessing what developments Centrum would need.
Skala-Coop stood at 1,990 forints on the BSE at 1055 GMT, down 10 forints.
